claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance and is susceptible to pesting at high temperature.
The proposed intervention is pack-cementation aluminizing with a graded interlayer at the alloy–coating interface.
The aluminizing treatment is to be performed at 900–1000 °C for 1–2 hours in an aluminum-rich powder pack.
The treatment will produce a thin, continuous, well-adherent alumina scale.
The treatment will produce a graded aluminum diffusion interlayer beneath the alumina scale.
The alumina scale will act as an oxygen-diffusion barrier.
The alumina scale will significantly reduce oxygen ingress into equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Reduced oxygen ingress will prevent pesting during the specified exposure.
The graded interlayer will reduce thermal-expansion mismatch at the coating–alloy interface.
The graded interlayer will mitigate thermal and mechanical interfacial stresses.
Mitigation of interfacial stresses will reduce alumina-scale spallation and cracking under service conditions.
Treated material will have markedly better oxidation resistance than untreated material during a 5-hour exposure to air at 800 °C.
Treated material will exhibit minimal oxide-scale spallation during the specified exposure.
The intervention will preserve high-temperature strength relative to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The intervention will preserve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The prediction is bounded to cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exposed to static air at 800 °C for 5 hours.
The prediction applies under mechanical loading at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
